title: "Lord, when my plans crumble and the path feels uncertain, help me trust that You are still writing redemption into my wilderness."
paragraphs: "Lord, when my plans crumble and the path feels uncertain, help me trust that You are still writing redemption into my wilderness."
When I read the Bible, I often imagine standing nearby, watching quietly.
The dust hangs heavy in the air as Moses runs—his future uncertain, his past behind him. I can almost feel the weight of that moment. One decision. One act. And suddenly everything changes.
He was raised in a palace, yet now he walks toward wilderness. What feels like exile… may actually be preparation.
I stand there as a witness, heart pounding—not because I am part of the story, but because I see how God works through broken, imperfect moments. Even mistakes cannot outrun divine purpose.
The desert is not the end. It is often where calling begins.

And I wonder…
What wilderness seasons in my life might actually be shaping something greater?
